_doc: Engine input per player, keyed by players.json id. `ipa` is fed to BlueTTS verbatim (RenikudPlus IPA: ˈ before the stressed vowel, ʁ χ ʔ ts dʒ tʃ). It spells speak_he (the text inside a trailing parenthetical, else the full name). The same IPA is used in the name clip and inside the match clip, so the two always sound alike.

`g2p` is what RenikudPlus produced on its own for the bare speak_he (kept to show what was changed). `why` explains each change. `stt_variants` are spellings the STT check accepts as the same pronunciation; never add a spelling that implies a different sound. `stt_text` replaces speak_he as the STT target when the intended pronunciation is deliberately spelled differently from the card. Optional `ipa_match` is the same pronunciation nudged for the match clip only (e.g. a vowel length). Optional `speed` overrides the global pace for that player (BlueTTS divides duration by it). Optional `listen` is a judgement call worth checking by ear; tts/listen.html highlights it.
A player missing from this file falls back to RenikudPlus G2P of speak_he and is flagged in the QA report.

fernand-mayembo.why: Congolese defender Fernand Mayembo: fer-NAN ma-YEM-bo, as in French. G2P said far-NAN me-AIM-bo. The STT drops the silent alef and writes מיימבו, which spells the same sounds.

chico-alves.why: Chico Alves: CHI-ko AL-ves. G2P dropped the e and read the ב as b (EL-bs; AL-bs on another call). The STT writes אלווס as often as אלבס, the same v. Not accepted: ציקו without the geresh, which would be TSI-ko.

lucas-falcao.why: Lucas Falcão: LU-kas fal-KAU (the Portuguese -ão as one diphthong). G2P said LO-kas pal-KA-u.

marcus-coco.why: Marcus Coco: MAR-kus KO-ko. G2P said KU-ko, as in the Hebrew קוקו (a ponytail). French stresses ko-KO; KO-ko is the natural Hebrew reading and was heard right 8/8 (ko-KO 7/8, A/B prescout-r1).
marcus-coco.listen: KO-ko (Hebrew stress) rather than the French ko-KO.

emmanuel-boateng.why: Ghanaian Emmanuel Boateng: e-ma-nu-EL bwa-TENG, ending in a plain ng as in English. G2P dropped the a (BO-teng). bo-A-teng was heard as בואטינג (ting) 8/8. With G2P's n+g ending the g came out as k (בואטנק) in a third of the takes; a bare ŋ passed 10/12, name clip 6/6 (A/B prescout-r1/r2, r3-boateng).
emmanuel-boateng.listen: bwa-TENG with an English ng. The STT heard the n+g ending as nk, so the g is not pronounced separately.

roei-alkukin.why: G2P correct (ro-I al-ku-KIN: the club, Wikipedia and FotMob all write Alkukin). Run together, the STT sometimes heard רויאל קוקין ('Royal'); a comma beat between the names lost the al instead (5/8 vs 7/8, A/B prescout-r2), so the name stays plain and best-of-8 picks the take.

daniel-dappa.why: G2P correct (da-ni-EL DA-pa; the club's English: Daniel Dappa).

andrian-kraev.why: Bulgarian Andrian Kraev: an-dri-YAN KRA-yev. G2P said AN-dri-yan KRAIV (one syllable). With the first-syllable stress the i was lost in 3/8 takes (STT: אנדרן); an-dri-YAN, which is also the Bulgarian stress, passed 8/8 (A/B prescout-r1).

stav-toriel.why: The club's English page writes Stav Toriel (to-ri-EL, G2P's reading); Wikipedia and FotMob write Stav Turiel (tu-ri-EL). The voice follows the media, as the earlier games follow how fans and commentators say a name. Both readings pass the STT 8/8, since טוריאל spells either (A/B prescout-r1/r2).
stav-toriel.listen: tu-ri-EL (Wikipedia, FotMob: Turiel) rather than the club's English to-ri-EL (Toriel). The alternative is rendered next to it.

omri-altman.why: G2P read עמרי as am-RI; the name is OM-ri (as in the Haifa game's עמרי גלזר). The STT adds a plene vav (עומרי), a spelling variant.

shahar-piven.why: G2P said FI-ben; Piven is PI-ven (the club's English: Shahar Piven).

douglas-owusu.why: Ghanaian Douglas Owusu: DA-glas o-VU-su (Hebrew דאגלס, as for Douglas Costa). G2P said DEG-las AV-su. A single v often vanished (STT: אוסו); doubled, like the hh trick, it stays (5/8 vs 4/8). An Akan w (o-WU-su) was heard worse (אורוסו, 2/8). The STT writes the v as אובוסו / אווסו, both the same sounds.
douglas-owusu.listen: o-VU-su with a v, as Hebrew writes it (אווסו); the Ghanaian name has a w (o-WU-su), which the STT heard worse.

yonatan-ferber.why: G2P correct (yo-na-TAN FER-ber; the club's English: Ferber).

el-yam-kancepolsky.why: El Yam Kancepolsky: el-YAM kan-tse-POL-ski (Polish c = ts). G2P read EL YAM as two stressed words and dropped the e of the surname (kants-POL-ski), which the STT then heard as קנספולסקי / קאנד ספולסקי. Said as one name, el-YAM, the surname comes back 8/8, but the STT writes the first name as אליאם / אליעם (the known name Eliam) in every take: the STT's prior for a near-homophone, like גרינברג for Haifa's גרימברג. Two separate words didn't fix it (4/16 heard אל ים) and garbled the surname (A/B prescout-r1/r2).
el-yam-kancepolsky.listen: el-YAM as one name. The STT always writes אליאם (Eliam) for it, never the card's אל ים; listen for el-YAM rather than e-li-AM.

tal-archel.why: TAL AR-chel. With G2P's ar-CHEL the second STT model heard טל הרצל ('Herzl') in 9/12 takes, and only 2/12 passed both models. With the first-syllable stress it never did: 12/12 on the second model, and 9/12 takes pass both (A/B r4-archel). A comma beat (טל, ארצ'ל) helped less (8/12).
tal-archel.listen: AR-chel (first-syllable stress); with the stress on -CHEL a second STT model kept hearing 'Herzl'.

yannick-leliendal.why: G2P kept (YA-nik le-LIN-dal), the Hebrew spelling's reading of the Dutch Leliendal. Both STT models drop the silent alefs (יניק, ללינדל) in every final clip, the same sounds, as Haifa's נובאקוביץ' came back נובקוביץ'.
